Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Summit Bancorp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Reynolds, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Reynolds:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Summit Bancorp's results for the third quarter of 2024. With me this morning are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; and David Wong, Chief Credit Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Summit Bancorp delivered strong performance in the third quarter, driven by our commitment to customer service and operational excellence.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Growing our core businesses
2. Investing in technology and innovation
3. Managing risk effectively
4. Optimizing our capital allocation
5. Enhancing our employee engagement.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on key areas. First, our net interest income showed solid year-over-year growth of 7.8% to $5.18 billion, though it dipped 1.9% sequentially, with the net interest margin expanding to 3.42%. Second, fee income across wealth management, investment banking, and cards grew robustly, with total non-interest income up significantly thanks to record inflows and deal momentum. Third, market conditions influenced non-interest income positively in areas like trading and markets amid volatility, offsetting some underwriting caution. Fourth, our revenue diversification efforts have meaningfully shifted our mix, with non-interest revenue now at 43% of total. Finally, looking ahead, we're guiding NII higher next quarter and core EPS ahead of consensus.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning. Summit Bancorp reported net income of $1.25 billion for the third quarter, or $1.78 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 3.2% year-over-year to $4.82 billion, flat sequentially from Q2, underscoring the resilience of our franchise despite a challenging rate environment with the Fed's terminal rate steady at 5.25-5.50% since July, pressuring deposit betas industry-wide. Our NIM expanded modestly to 3.48% from 3.42% in Q2, down 12 basis points year-over-year, thanks to a favorable mix shift: C&I loans grew 4.1% quarter-over-quarter to $185 billion at 5.75% yields, focused on high-quality tech and healthcare in Southeast and California markets. Mortgage warehouse lines, a core strength like at JPMorgan and Wells Fargo, expanded 6% to $42 billion yielding over 6.2%, offsetting softer consumer demand.

Average deposits grew 2.8% year-over-year to $312 billion, loan-to-deposit ratio steady at 92%, with retail deposit betas peaking at 65%—below the street average of 75% at regionals like KeyCorp—as money market competition eased with yields at 5.1%. Wholesale funding costs rose 5 basis points to 4.85%, managed by $25 billion in short-duration FHLB advances, supporting LCR of 125% and NSFR at 112%.

Regionally, Southeast markets like Atlanta, Charlotte, and Nashville drove 55% of NII growth with NIM at 3.62%, boosted by non-interest-bearing deposits at 28% of total, up from 26%. West Coast tech corridor C&I yields stayed firm on venture debt, while we trimmed CRE office to 4.5% of loans, ahead of peers, down $1.2 billion. Asia-Pacific wealth deposits via Singapore added $8 billion quarter-over-quarter at 2.1% blended cost, diversifying U.S. rate risks.

Key initiatives included our AI-powered dynamic pricing engine across 70% of commercial portfolio, optimizing yields 15 basis points via real-time risk-adjusted repricing, akin to Goldman Sachs' Marcus enhancements. We also swapped $10 billion of lower-yielding securities into 4.8% two-year Treasuries, lifting portfolio yield to 3.95% and duration to 4.2 years for rate-cut protection.

Diving deeper into NII trends, interest income reached $9.42 billion, up 10.2% year-over-year and 0.8% quarter-over-quarter, from 6.5% average loan growth to $412 billion, including 12% C&I expansion in healthcare and tech with $15 billion new commitments year-to-date. Consumer loans rose 4%, securities yields up 15 basis points to 4.25%. Interest expense climbed to $4.24 billion, up 15.4% year-over-year and 5.1% sequentially, from deposit betas at 68%, with core low-cost deposits at 42%. Southeast NII grew 11% on 9% loans in Florida and Texas via de novo branches and SoFi-like fintech ties; Northeast CRE paydowns slowed growth, but multifamily strong; Europe wholesale up 14% on EURIBOR loans.

Balance sheet optimization redeployed $12 billion to higher-spread C&I, adding 4 basis points to NIM; AI deposit pricing retained 92% core deposits; 60% fixed-rate loans swapped to floating for Fed easing.

Turning to non-interest income, it totaled $2.8 billion, up 8% year-over-year and 32% of revenue, up from 30%, resilient amid inflation, high rates, geopolitics, and tech-led equity rally. Investment banking fees at $850 million, up 12%, with advisory up 22% to $420 million on $35 billion deals like consumer staples mergers; underwriting down 5% to $310 million on cautious IPOs; EMEA lagged, APAC up 18%. AI deal-sourcing boosted mid-market opportunities.

Markets revenues $1.1 billion, up 15%, FICC $650 million on rates/credit amid VIX at 18 and curve steepening; equities $450 million on AI stocks; quant strategies added alpha. AUM $1.7 trillion, wealth fees $520 million up 6% on $45 billion inflows, equities lift; ETF launches and ESG tools. Cards $330 million up 4% on 7% volumes, digital wallets; LatAm upside, blockchain remittances.

Fee income specifically hit $1.9 billion, up 16%, 28% of revenue. Wealth management $1.1 billion, up 18%, AUM $4.2 trillion with $45 billion inflows on generational transfer; advisory up 22%, ESG/alternatives surge, WealthGPT robo-advisor for 2.5 million clients; Asia-Pacific 25% growth. Investment banking $550 million up 25%, M&A $280 million on $150 billion volumes, ECM $140 million; IBX platform, adjacency expansion. Cards $250 million up 9%, interchange $160 million on 1.2 billion swipes; tokenization, Shopify BNPL.

Our diversification initiatives propelled total revenue to $14.2 billion, up 8%, NII 57% down from 68%, non-interest $6.1 billion up 22% at 43%. Wealth $2.4 billion up 28%, GlobalWealth Digital with Aladdin; payments $1.8 billion up 25% via EuroPay acquisition, PayFlow API; capital markets $1.2 billion up 19%; embedded finance $700 million up 55% with BNPL, tokenization. Impact: 65% of 12% EPS growth, RoTE to 13.2%, volatility down 20%.

Key performance indicators include ROTCE at 18%, CET1 at 11.8%, efficiency ratio improving to 57%. For Q4 guidance, NII $4.85-$4.95 billion, 1-3% sequential, 4-6% year-over-year, assuming one 25 basis point Fed cut, NIM 3.45-3.50%, balance sheet growth. Core EPS $1.72-$1.82 ahead of $1.75 consensus, PPNR $6.1-$6.3 billion, fees up 8%, expenses $3.85-$3.95 billion, provisions $950 million-$1.05 billion, NCOs 45 basis points, FICO 735. Full-year NII $20.8-$21.2 billion, fees $7.5-$7.8 billion.

We're positioning for higher-for-longer with fee target 35% by 2026, CRE under 15%, BaaS with fintechs for 10% deposit growth.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. As Chief Risk Officer, I would like to briefly discuss our risk management framework. We continue to prioritize proactive risk identification and mitigation. Our key focus areas include credit risk in commercial real estate portfolios, particularly office exposure, and operational risks from cybersecurity and third-party fintech partnerships. We remain vigilant in monitoring emerging risks like geopolitical tensions and regulatory changes such as Basel III endgame, adapting our strategies accordingly with stress testing and AI-enhanced early warning systems.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, that is 1 then the pound sign. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Good morning. Can you provide more detail on NII trends, particularly the YoY and QoQ dynamics and how you're managing deposit betas?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, Mike. As Michael outlined, the 7.8% YoY NII growth to $5.18 billion reflects strong loan expansion in C&I and consumer, despite a 1.9% QoQ dip from paydowns and repricing. Deposit betas at 68% are contained via our AI pricing engine, retaining core deposits at 42% mix. Regionally, Southeast strength offsets CRE headwinds, and hedges position us for cuts. We're confident in Q4 growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
What are your expectations for fee income breakdown, especially wealth management and investment banking performance drivers going forward?

Michael Chen:
Great question, Emily. Wealth management fees up 18% to $1.1 billion on record AUM and inflows, driven by advisory shifts, ESG products, and WealthGPT; expect 10-12% FY growth. Investment banking up 25% on M&A resurgence and ECM tailwinds, league table gains; guide 15-20% full-year. Cards steady on volumes. Diversification keeps us resilient.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera:
Can you comment on the credit quality of the commercial real estate portfolio amid market conditions?

David Wong:
Thanks, Tom. Credit quality remains strong, with CECL reserves at 1.25%, NCOs at 45 basis points stable versus peers, consumer FICO at 735. We've proactively trimmed CRE office to 4.5%, focusing on multifamily and industrial at high occupancy. Diversified sectors like tech/healthcare C&I support low delinquencies at 1.8% overall, 20 basis points below peers.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Sarah Thompson for any closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your interest in Summit Bancorp. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
